subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The prescribed root cause fix was NOT implemented. The file is still a bare createContext with a static default value — there is no ContentstackProvider component, no useState for reactive content, no useEffect subscribing to Stack.livePreview.on('entryUpdate', ...), and no state setter callback. Without these, the context value never changes after initial render, so no downstream consumer (236+ components using useContent) can ever receive live preview updates. Every acceptance criterion — real-time text update without reload, prompt appearance, partial update of only changed content, no flicker, GO/UP/MX variant support, no stale values — is unmet because the reactivity mechanism is entirely absent.
issues.suggestedFix: Implement the prescribed minimal fix: create a ContentstackProvider component that wraps createContext. Replace the static value with useState initialized from defaultContent. Add a useEffect that calls Stack.livePreview.on('entryUpdate', callback) using the existing @contentstack/delivery-sdk config already used in getStaticProps helpers (getSingletonEntry/getSingleEntry). On each entryUpdate callback, call the state setter with the updated content so all useContent consumers re-render. Export both the context and the provider.

issues.description: TypeScript strict compliance: the interface uses untyped `any` — `footer?: [any]` — without an explanatory comment. This violates the strict typing requirement.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace `[any]` with the proper Contentstack footer interface type, or if the type is genuinely unknown during migration, add an explanatory comment and use `[unknown]` or a dedicated `IContentstackFooter` interface.

issues.description: useContent calls useContext(ContentstackContext) but there is no Provider component in the codebase that supplies a reactive value. Even if a provider were added at the app root, the current architecture has no integration point. The hook will always return the static default `{}` from createContext, meaning getContentByKey will always return defaultValue. No live preview can propagate through this hook as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Once ContentstackProvider is implemented (see blocker above), ensure the app's root layout wraps children with <ContentstackProvider defaultContent={...}>. The useContent hook itself does not need changes — it already depends on [content] in its useCallback dependency array, so it will correctly re-render when the context value updates. Verify the provider is mounted in _app.tsx or the equivalent Next.js root.

issues.description: getContentByKey is called with `{} as IContentstackLink` as the default value. If the context is not yet populated or the key is missing, this casts an empty object to IContentstackLink, which may cause runtime errors when CustomLink tries to render href=undefined. With live preview enabled, transient states during content updates could briefly expose this path. No error boundary or null-check guards against malformed content during a preview push.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a guard: if href is falsy, render children without a link or return null. Alternatively, provide a meaningful default or throw a ConfigError for missing required content keys during development.
